feature.title: UI design system and enhanced graphics cleanup
feature.request: Clean up all the UI elements and make them look nicer. Context: We have continued to build up the UI for this application, adding plenty of buttons and modals, but we never stepped back to create a proper design system. Requirements: -Come up with a design system (or implement a current one) that matches the general vibes of the current site -The theme should stay similar to what it is right now. Simple, dark gray with blue accents. No gradients. Basic, old-internet, utilitarian, but with a modern twist -Ensure all interactable elements have the correct cursor -Clean up the noise output bar that's in the audio settings, right now there isn't a very clean animation so it looks choppy -Clean up the enhanced graphics settings: a) not obvious whether it's turned on or not b) not obvious whether it's recommended (maybe show a modal initially that recommends turning it on, then store in cookies so it doesn't show again?) c) janky organization on the main landing and in the visualizer settings menu. Scope and non-goals: -changing functionality. Verification: -Organized design system that is reused automatically across app -Uses best UI/UX standards -enhanced graphics cleaned up

problem.statement: The UI grew ad hoc: three styling approaches (Tailwind utilities, buttonStyles.ts constants, ControlPanel.module.css with hex colors), no color or radius tokens in app.css, a gradient on landing cards, buttons and labels without a pointer cursor (Tailwind 4 preflight sets none), a level meter that steps at 10 Hz, and an enhanced graphics toggle (on origin/main) whose on/off state, recommendation and placement are unclear.
users: Viewers who pick an audio source on the landing page and tune a visualizer in its settings panel
Contributors adding new controls or dialogs, who need one obvious set of styles to reuse
evidence: ControlPanel.module.css uses #333/#555 buttons, a second button look next to buttonStyles.ts blue-600
useLevelMeter.ts setInterval 100 ms with no CSS transition on the bar in ActiveSourcePanel.tsx
Tailwind 4 preflight has no cursor pointer for button; dialog buttons, switch label and select lack it

goals: One token-based design system in app/app.css @theme (dark gray surfaces, one blue accent, flat, no gradients, one radius and focus ring) plus shared primitives (Button, Switch, Dialog, Panel/Section, Field, Select, Range) that every screen uses
Every interactable element shows the correct cursor (pointer; not-allowed when disabled; default for plain text)
The audio level meter animates smoothly with no visible stepping

Enhanced graphics shows its on/off state unmistakably, is marked Recommended, is offered once by a first-visit landing modal, and sits in a consistent place on the landing page and in the settings panel
non_goals: No functional change: no new settings, no change to audio, rhythm, scene behavior or stored values other than the one new dismissal flag
No external UI library or new runtime dependency
No change to three.js scenes, shaders or the enhanced graphics render paths
No light theme or theme switcher
Enhanced graphics UX changes are proposals: the implementer presents them to the user before building them
success_metrics: Zero color literals in UI className strings, app.css outside tokens and CSS Modules (scene palettes, control defaults and DevTelemetryOverlay exempt)
The e2e cursor sweep passes on every AC2 surface; the lint rule is a secondary guard
A unit spec asserts the meter transition and reduced-motion; the PR records the manual smoothness check
axe has no serious violations on the landing page, source dialog, settings panel and the new modal
constraints: Tailwind 4 tokens live in app/app.css @theme; CSS Modules only where real CSS is needed (conventions.md)
Named exports only; comments explain why; specs next to files, 95% coverage
Total CSS budget 6.1 kB gzip and JS budgets in .size-limit.json; any raise justified in the PR
Visual baselines are Linux-only and regenerated by the Update visual snapshots workflow
Enhanced graphics code exists only on origin/main; implementation branches from origin/main and first confirms the real store and hook
A first-run modal must not block e2e specs: fixtures seed the dismissal flag
Meter must not setState per animation frame (rule 3); smoothing via CSS transition or a ref-driven style update

acceptance_criteria.then: it uses a transform transition whose duration is at least the meter interval and none under prefers-reduced-motion (asserted by a unit spec), state still updates only at the existing throttle, and a manual dev check recorded in the PR finds no visible stepping; if it still steps, a requestAnimationFrame ref-driven lerp replaces the transition with no setState

acceptance_criteria.when: the user looks at enhanced graphics
acceptance_criteria.then: a switch shows On or Off in text and color, a Recommended label is visible, and the control sits in the same named section position in both places

decisions.question: Where is the dismissed recommendation remembered?
When does the one-time enhanced graphics recommendation appear?
decisions.answer: On the first visit to the landing page; choosing or dismissing stores the answer

decisions.question: How deep is the design system?
decisions.answer: Tailwind theme tokens plus a small set of shared primitive components used by every screen

decisions.question: May the PR regenerate visual baselines and adjust the size budget?
decisions.answer: Yes, both expected, justified in the PR description

decisions.question: Where does the enhanced graphics code come from?
decisions.answer: It exists on origin/main; the implementation branches from origin/main and the first slice records the real store, hook and UI locations
decisions.rationale: Local checkout has no enhanced graphics code

decisions.question: May enhanced graphics UX changes be built automatically?
decisions.answer: No: the plan recommends them, and the implementer confirms the concrete design with the user before building that slice

decisions.question: Does the landing card gradient go?
decisions.answer: Yes, replaced by a flat solid caption band, as no gradients is a requirement

decisions.question: How are options weighted?
decisions.answer: UX and fit weigh most (30 each), effort least (10), because the request is about polish and a design system that is reused automatically, not speed

decisions.question: How is the meter smoothed?
decisions.answer: Keep the 10 Hz throttled state in useLevelMeter; the bar uses transform scaleX with a linear transition equal to the tick interval, none under prefers-reduced-motion; no per-frame setState and no hook signature change
decisions.rationale: Rule 3 forbids per-frame state; a transition matched to the tick makes motion continuous at no render cost

options.summary: Add color/radius/focus tokens to app.css @theme, replace buttonStyles.ts and the module's button/form rules with a handful of tiny primitives, add one global cursor rule, drive the meter with a CSS transition, and add one enhanced-graphics Switch plus a first-visit modal reusing the existing dialog pattern.
approach: Slice 0: branch from origin/main; record the real enhanced graphics store/hook/UI locations (docs/plans/*-enhanced-graphics/ describe only the planned contract: key audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphics, enhancedGraphicsStore.ts, useEnhancedGraphics.ts; confirm against real code).

app.css: add @theme tokens (--color-surface, --color-surface-raised, --color-border, --color-accent, --color-accent-hover, --color-text, --radius-ui) and @layer base rule: button, summary, select, input[type=checkbox|range|color], label[for], a {cursor:pointer} and :disabled {cursor:not-allowed}; one :focus-visible ring using accent.

Create app/components/ui/ with Button (variants primary/outline), Switch (role=switch, visible On/Off text + accent color), Dialog (extracted from AudioSourceDialog: overlay, focus, Escape), Section, Field. Replace buttonStyles.ts; restyle ControlPanel.module.css to var(--color-*) tokens only, keep ControlInput native elements but wrapped by Field.
Swap hex/gradient literals: VisualizationCard flat solid caption band (D8), LandingPage bg and dialog colors use tokens; stats overlays keep documented mono palette.
Meter: keep useLevelMeter 10 Hz setState; add transition-[width] duration-100 ease-linear on the bar (motion-reduce:transition-none).

Enhanced graphics: one EnhancedGraphicsSetting using Switch with a Recommended badge, placed in a section titled Graphics at the top of both landing and settings panel; EnhancedGraphicsPrompt modal (Dialog) with Turn on / Not now, writing audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphicsPromptSeen via storage.ts wrappers and calling the existing toggle; present to user before building (D6).

Guards: a lint rule (no-restricted-syntax on raw <button className> in app/) plus a grep spec for color literals; e2e cursor sweep over interactive elements; seed the flag in e2e/fixtures.ts; axe on new modal; regenerate baselines.

options.summary: Token layer in app.css @theme plus a typed, enforced primitives library (app/components/ui) where cursor, focus, disabled and a11y are built in once, a ref-driven meter, and a guarded first-visit modal, with lint and e2e gates preventing regression.
approach: Slice 0: branch from origin/main; record the real enhanced graphics store, hook and UI locations (docs/plans/*-enhanced-graphics/ is the planned contract only: key audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphics, enhancedGraphicsStore.ts, useEnhancedGraphics.ts). Confirm before relying on them.

Tokens: app.css @theme adds surface-0/1/2, border, text, text-muted, accent, accent-hover, danger, radius-ui, ring; base layer sets cursor:pointer for button/summary/select/label[for]/input[type=range|checkbox], not-allowed for :disabled and aria-disabled.

Primitives in app/components/ui: Button (variant primary|secondary|ghost, size), Switch (role=switch, visible On/Off text plus color), Dialog (native focus trap, Escape, labelled, shared by source dialog and new modal), Panel/Section, Field, Select, Range, Badge. Each has a spec. Migrate buttonStyles.ts and ControlPanel.module.css into them and delete the module.

Meter: useLevelMeter keeps the 100 ms throttle but writes the level to a ref and a CSS custom property or transform: scaleX on the bar, with a 100 ms linear transition and prefers-reduced-motion fallback; no per-frame setState.
EnhancedGraphicsSection: one component rendering Switch, Recommended Badge and help text, mounted as the first named section in both landing and settings panel.

First-visit modal: storage.ts gets a guarded read/write for audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphicsPromptSeen (try/catch, private mode shows nothing). Turn on or Not now calls the existing setter, then writes the flag. Fixtures seed the flag.

Guards: ESLint no-restricted-syntax rule flags raw button, select and input[type=range] JSX and color literals outside ui and app.css; e2e cursor sweep over all interactive elements; axe on every surface; flat solid caption band replaces the card gradient.

options.summary: Design the system around what people see and feel: one shared EnhancedGraphicsControl (switch with On/Off text, Recommended badge, same named 'Graphics' section) in landing and panel, a once-only first-visit modal, and a CSS-transition meter, all on tokenized primitives.
approach: Tokens in app.css @theme: surface-0/1/2, border, text, text-muted, accent (one blue), accent-fg, danger, radius-md, focus ring; remove the card gradient for a solid caption band; delete hex colors from ControlPanel.module.css.

Primitives in app/components/ui/ (Button primary/secondary/ghost, Switch, Dialog, Section, Field, Select, Range). Base layer in app.css gives button, summary, select, label[for], input[type=range|checkbox], a, [role=switch] cursor-pointer and :disabled/[aria-disabled] not-allowed, so even new raw elements are correct.
Switch: role=switch, aria-checked, visible text 'On'/'Off' beside a track that is accent-filled when on and gray when off; never color alone; disabled state dimmed with not-allowed cursor.

EnhancedGraphicsControl (Switch + 'Recommended' badge + one-line hint) rendered inside a Section titled 'Graphics' as the first section on the landing page (beside Connect audio) and the first section in the settings panel, so position and name match (AC4). Binds to the existing toggle/hook confirmed on origin/main.

First-visit modal on Dialog: title 'Turn on enhanced graphics?', one sentence of benefit, primary 'Turn on', secondary 'Not now'. Focus lands on Turn on, Escape equals Not now, focus returns to the page. Either choice writes audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphicsPromptSeen in localStorage via storage.ts and applies the value through the existing toggle. Storage failure: show nothing broken, do not loop.

Meter: keep 10 Hz useLevelMeter; ActiveSourcePanel bar uses transform scaleX or width with transition ~100ms linear (matches tick interval so motion is continuous), disabled under prefers-reduced-motion; role=meter with aria-valuenow updated at the throttle rate only.

Guardrails: lint/spec scanning app/ for color literals and raw 'button' class strings; e2e sweep of all interactive elements asserting computed cursor; fixtures seed the seen flag; axe on landing, source dialog, panel, new modal.

decision_rationale: O4 keeps O1's cheap, convention-fitting base (tokens in app.css, a base-layer cursor rule, a transition-only meter) but adds what O1 lacks for the verification bar: a full primitive set enforced by lint, so the system is reused automatically, and O3's single Graphics section so enhanced graphics is clear and identically placed. It costs more effort than O1, which weighs least here (D9).

design.overview: A token layer in app/app.css @theme (surface-0/1/2 dark grays, border, text, text-muted, one blue accent and accent-hover, danger, one radius, a focus ring) plus a base layer that gives every native interactive element the right cursor and focus-visible ring. A small primitives library in app/components/ui renders every button, switch, dialog, section, field, select, range and badge from those tokens. All screens migrate onto it; buttonStyles.ts goes and ControlPanel.module.css keeps only layout that needs real CSS, in tokens. A lint rule keeps raw controls and color literals out of feature code. The meter animates with a transition. Enhanced graphics gets one control, placed first in a Graphics section in both places, and a once-only landing modal, built only after the user approves the concrete design.

contracts.name: Design tokens
contracts.definition: app.css @theme names: --color-surface-0, --color-surface-1, --color-surface-2, --color-border, --color-text, --color-text-muted, --color-accent, --color-accent-hover, and status-only --color-success, --color-warning, --color-danger (meter level and silence cue use success and warning), --radius-ui; used as Tailwind utilities. contracts.name: Primitive props
contracts.definition: Button extends button attributes plus variant primary|secondary|ghost and size sm|md; Switch {checked, onCheckedChange, label, disabled} renders a native input type=checkbox role=switch with label[for] so existing role and name selectors keep working; Dialog {open, onClose, title, children} keeps role=dialog and the title as accessible name (source dialog stays 'Audio source'); Section {title, children}; Field {label, htmlFor, children} uses label[for]; Select and Range are native select and input range; Badge {children}. Named exports from app/components/ui.

contracts.name: Prompt seen flag
contracts.definition: localStorage key audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphicsPromptSeen, value '1', through storage.ts wrappers that never throw. The prompt shows only when the flag is absent, no enhanced graphics value is stored and storage works. Turn on sets the toggle on; Not now and Escape only write the flag.

contracts.name: Enhanced graphics binding
contracts.definition: EnhancedGraphicsControl and the prompt read and set the toggle only through the existing hook on origin/main (planned useEnhancedGraphics, key audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphics, default off); frozen in S0 against the real code, unchanged

design.data: One new localStorage value (C3). Nothing else stored or changed.
design.ux: Flat dark grays with one blue accent, 1px borders, a single small radius, Inter, monospace kept for stats overlays: utilitarian, old-internet structure with modern spacing and focus rings. Primary actions blue filled, secondary bordered gray, ghost text-only. Switch shows On/Off in text and color. Enhanced graphics lives first in a Graphics section with a Recommended badge in both places. Modal appears once on first landing visit, after first paint.
design.accessibility: Switch is a native checkbox with role=switch, aria-checked implied, and visible On/Off text; Dialog labelled, focus trapped, Escape and focus return, page inert behind it; focus-visible ring on every primitive; role=meter with aria-valuenow is added to the bar as new markup at the throttle rate; reduced motion disables the meter transition; axe on landing, source dialog, settings panel and the modal.
design.security_privacy: No new data leaves the browser; one boolean in localStorage.
design.observability: None beyond existing console-error e2e fixtures.
design.rollout: One branch cut from origin/main for everything. PR1 refactor(ui): S0, S1, S2, S3, S7, S8, S4, S6 (tokens, primitives, migration including the existing enhanced graphics UI restyled in place, guard, meter, its own baseline regeneration and budget). PR2 feat(ui): S5 and S9, started only after contracts.md exists and the user approves Q1 (D6), with a second baseline regeneration. Rollback by revert or Cloudflare rollback; the seen flag is harmless if left behind.

test_strategy.unit: Spec per primitive (variants, disabled, Switch toggling and text, Dialog Escape and focus return), storage wrappers for C3 including a throwing localStorage, prompt shows once and applies the chosen value, meter bar style and reduced-motion class.
test_strategy.integration: renderWithProviders: landing and ControlPanel render EnhancedGraphicsControl first in a Graphics section; lint rule spec via RuleTester or a fixture file.
test_strategy.e2e: Existing specs pass; one shared addInitScript helper seeds C3 and is used by fixtures.ts, visual.spec.ts and a11y.spec.ts; a dedicated unseeded-context spec covers the modal; the cursor sweep covers landing, source dialog, modal and a visualizer route with panel and fullscreen controls; axe on the modal; baselines regenerated per PR and reviewed.
test_strategy.manual: npm run dev: watch the meter for stepping, hover every control, check enhanced graphics in both places and the modal once, console clean.
test_strategy.non_functional: Measure gzip CSS after S1 and record the delta, again after S8; npm run size and lighthouse on a fresh profile pass, any raise justified in the PR.

open_questions.question: Does the user approve the concrete enhanced graphics control, placement and modal copy from S0, and should the Recommended badge and modal be conditional on any capability gating S0 found?
open_questions.owner: user, asked by the implementer before S5

findings.finding: S3 migrates ControlPanel, landing and the settings panel but depends only on S2, not on S0. Enhanced graphics UI already exists on origin/main (D5) and is absent from this checkout. If S1 to S4 are built before S0 confirms the real code, the existing enhanced graphics toggle is either missed by the migration, so the lint guard and the AC1 and AC7 grep fail on it, or it collides at merge. The plan also never says S1 to S4 branch from origin/main. The local HEAD (c03849a) and origin/main may have diverged.
findings.suggestion: Make S0 the first slice and have S1 to S4 depend on it. State that the whole branch is cut from origin/main. S3's scope must list the real enhanced graphics UI files that S0 records. S5 then only restructures them.
findings.resolution: S0 is first, the branch is cut from origin/main, S1 and S7 depend on S0, and S7 migrates the existing enhanced graphics UI files S0 records.

findings.finding: AC5 says either choice 'applies the chosen value through the existing toggle'. For a returning user who already enabled enhanced graphics before the flag existed, the stored audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphics value is on but the new seen-flag is absent. The modal then appears on their first visit after deploy, and 'Not now' would switch their setting off. That is a functional change, which conflicts with the non-goal 'no functional change'. The plan also does not say what happens when the toggle is unsupported or off on a device that cannot run it.
findings.suggestion: Add to AC5 and C3: do not show the modal when an explicit enhancedGraphics value is already stored or the setting is already on. 'Not now' only writes the seen flag and leaves the setting unchanged (or sets off only if it was unset). Add a unit case for a pre-existing stored on value.
findings.resolution: AC5 and C3: no modal when an enhanced graphics value is stored; Not now and Escape only write the flag; unit case for a pre-existing on value.

findings.finding: AC3 and the success metric ('no jump larger than the transition step at 60 fps in the dev check') are not testable. Nothing defines 'step' or 'visible stepping', and no automated check is named. D10 keeps a 100 ms linear transition on a 100 ms setInterval. Interval jitter and a transition that always lags one tick behind the reading leave the bar changing direction abruptly at each tick. The level comes from a noisy analyser, so it may still read as choppy (K, O1 risk 'may look slightly laggy'). The plan also claims 'role=meter values at the throttle rate', but the current bar in ActiveSourcePanel.tsx:29-34 has no role=meter or aria-valuenow, so this is new markup and is not covered by an AC.
findings.suggestion: Define AC3 observably: the bar element has a transform transition and a duration at least equal to METER_INTERVAL_MS. Add a unit assertion on the style or class and reduced-motion, plus a manual 'looks smooth' check recorded in the PR. If the linear 100 ms transition still looks choppy, fall back to a requestAnimationFrame ref-driven lerp, which needs no setState. Say explicitly whether role=meter is being added.
findings.resolution: AC3 made observable (transition duration, reduced motion, unit spec, recorded manual check) with a rAF ref lerp fallback; role=meter declared as new markup in accessibility.

findings.finding: The success metric 'zero hex or arbitrary color literals in app/ outside app.css tokens and the stats overlays' is false in the repo. A grep of non-spec files in app/ finds hex or rgb or 0x literals in visualizer scene and control files (bassInkControls.ts, cubesControls.ts, dancingCharacterConfig.ts, formations.ts, useCubesScene.ts and others) and in DevTelemetryOverlay.tsx. Those are scene palettes, which a non-goal forbids touching. As written, AC1 and the lint or grep guard either fail or force edits to the three.js scenes.
findings.suggestion: Scope AC1, the metric and the guard to UI styling only: className strings, CSS and CSS Modules, plus the UI files under app/components and app/features/*/components. Explicitly exempt scene, control-default and telemetry files. Add DevTelemetryOverlay to the migrated screens or the exemption list.
findings.resolution: AC1, the success metric and the guard scoped to UI styling; scenes, control defaults and DevTelemetryOverlay exempt.

findings.finding: The theme is 'dark gray with a single blue accent', but the meter bar uses bg-green-500 and bg-yellow-500 (ActiveSourcePanel.tsx:31) and the plan defines only a --color-danger token. AC7 ('single blue accent') and the color guard give no rule for status colors (meter ok or silent, warnings, SilenceWarning). The implementer will either break AC7 or lose the silent-source cue. Also, the existing normalize control is an input[type=checkbox][role=switch]. The new Switch primitive presumably replaces it, and the plan says nothing about whether existing e2e selectors, accessible names and the 'Show performance stats' checkbox (fullscreen.spec.ts:94) keep working.
findings.suggestion: Add --color-success and --color-warning (or an explicit rule that the meter uses accent and warn) to C1 and allow them as status colors in AC7. State that Switch keeps the native input role=switch (or that the role and name selectors used by the e2e specs are unchanged), and that Select and Field keep native select and label[for] so getByLabel and selectOption still work.
findings.resolution: C1 adds success and warning status tokens; AC7 allows status hues; C2 keeps native checkbox role=switch, label[for], native select and range so selectors hold.

findings.finding: Two PRs but baselines and AC6 are tied to S6, which depends on S5 (PR2). The rollout says PR1 includes 'baselines and any justified CSS budget raise'. S6 sits after S5, so the order is contradictory. Baselines are Linux-only and regenerated by a workflow, so PR1 needs one regeneration and PR2 a second. The first-visit modal also lands in landing.png unless the visual spec seeds the flag, and the plan only mentions seeding in e2e/fixtures.ts. Landing-dependent specs (connectAudio, deep-links, a11y) have different entry points. A missed one fails with a modal overlay rather than an obvious error.
findings.suggestion: Split S6 into S6a (PR1: budget, baselines, size check) and S6b (PR2: re-baseline, lighthouse on a fresh profile). Seed the flag with one shared addInitScript path used by fixtures.ts, visual.spec.ts and a11y.spec.ts, with a dedicated unseeded-context spec only for the modal.
findings.resolution: S6 is PR1's baselines and budget; S9 is PR2's; one shared seeding helper used by fixtures, visual and a11y specs.

findings.finding: The 'Recommended' badge is static and unconditional. The user asked 'whether it's recommended', which may depend on device or capability, and a modal that recommends turning on a heavier render path for every first-time visitor (phones, no WebGL2, low-end GPUs) is a performance-risk claim made with no evidence. S0 only records locations, not whether origin/main has any capability or performance gating.
findings.suggestion: Add to S0: record any capability or performance gating the existing enhanced graphics code has. Make the badge and modal conditional on that, or put the unconditional-recommendation choice to the user explicitly in Q1.
findings.resolution: S0 records capability gating; K7 added; Q1 asks the user whether the badge and modal are conditional.

findings.finding: The Dialog primitive is extracted from AudioSourceDialog.tsx, which e2e finds by the accessible name 'Audio source', and it must still pass expectNoA11yViolations. The plan lists focus trap and focus return but not stacking. The first-visit modal and 'Connect audio' are on the same landing page, and dismissal while the source dialog is open, or two tabs opening, is not handled. The O2 risk 'native dialog differences break e2e selectors' dropped out of the O4 risk list. The C4 contract is also 'frozen in S0 against real code', but S0's only output (docs/plans/ui-design-system/contracts.md) is a draft path and nothing checks it.
findings.suggestion: Add a risk for the Dialog extraction and keep title, role and name unchanged for the source dialog. Define that the prompt does not render while another dialog is open, and have it appear only after the first paint with the landing controls inert behind it. Add a gate: S5 cannot start until contracts.md exists and Q1 is answered.
findings.resolution: K6 added; C2 keeps the source dialog role and name; AC5 says the prompt does not render while another dialog is open; S5 gated on contracts.md and Q1.

findings.finding: S3 is a size-L slice that migrates every screen, deletes buttonStyles.ts and ControlPanel hex colors, adds the lint rule and adds the cursor sweep, all at once. The lint rule fails on any unmigrated file, and AC6 is tested only at the end. Review risk is high with full baseline churn (K4), and R1 is probably honest only if the slice is split. K5 rates lint false positives low, but no-restricted-syntax on raw button or select JSX cannot see class strings built as variables or the ControlInput native elements already wrapped by Field.
findings.suggestion: Split S3 into S3a (landing, cards, dialog, audio settings), S3b (ControlPanel and ControlInput) and S3c (guard: lint rule plus the cursor sweep, added last so it turns on only when everything is migrated). Keep the e2e cursor sweep as the primary check and the lint rule secondary.
findings.resolution: S3 split into S3 (landing and audio), S7 (panel) and S8 (guard, last).

findings.finding: AC2 lists elements and requires an e2e sweep, but 'any page of the app' includes the visualizer route, the fullscreen controls and the ControlPanel summary and details sections. The plan only sweeps landing, source dialog and one settings panel. Disabled-state coverage ('not-allowed') and aria-disabled on non-native elements are not shown to exist in the UI at all. The CSS budget (6.1 kB) already has a margin problem: the base layer plus eight primitives plus tokens is the largest unmeasured risk, yet K2 rates the impact as low and measures only after S1 and S3.
findings.suggestion: State the swept routes in AC2 (landing, visualizer route with panel open, source dialog, modal). Measure gzip CSS after S1 and record a delta, not only after S3, so the budget decision is not left to the end. Raise K2's impact to medium.
findings.resolution: AC2 names the swept surfaces; CSS measured after S1; K2 impact raised to medium.
